title: Skill installation distinguishes installation, refusal, and explicit update
expectation: Install creates the complete bundled tree, refuses a second non-forced installation without changing any files, and --force restores modified entrypoint and topic contents exactly to the CLI-bundled versions.

checks.command: monochange skill install --dir .eval-skill && monochange skill read monochange > .entry-original && monochange skill read configuration > .config-original && cmp .entry-original .eval-skill/SKILL.md && cmp .config-original .eval-skill/skills/configuration.md && test -f .eval-skill/examples/readme.md && test -f .eval-skill/skills/commands.md
checks.why: A successful installation must provide real bundled content and linked supporting documents.

checks.command: printf 'Local edited skill\n' > .eval-skill/SKILL.md; printf 'Local edited topic\n' > .eval-skill/skills/configuration.md; monochange skill install --dir .eval-skill > .refusal.out 2>&1; rc=$?; cat .refusal.out; test $rc -eq 1 && grep -q 'pass --force to replace it' .refusal.out && test "$(cat .eval-skill/SKILL.md)" = 'Local edited skill' && test "$(cat .eval-skill/skills/configuration.md)" = 'Local edited topic'
checks.why: Refusal must preserve both the user's entrypoint edits and topic edits.
Explicit update must refresh supporting modules as well as the entrypoint.
